title: Vegetable Frittata
description: A thick, tender oven-finished frittata with potatoes, bell pepper, spinach and cheddar. Good hot, warm or cold the next day.
scaleNote: This fills a 10-inch oven-safe skillet. For a larger batch, bake it in a greased {len 9x13 in} dish for 25 to 30 minutes.
equipment: {len 10 in} oven-safe nonstick or cast-iron skillet

image.alt: A golden vegetable frittata in a skillet, cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 375F oven} with a rack in the middle. Whisk the eggs, milk, half the salt, the pepper and three-quarters of the cheese in a bowl.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the potato and the rest of the salt, cover and cook, stirring now and then, until tender and lightly golden, {time 8-10 min}.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook uncovered until soft, {time 4-5 min}. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, {time 1 min}. Spread the vegetables evenly.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables and cook without stirring until the edges begin to set, {time 2-3 min}. Scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake until the center is set and no longer jiggles, {time 12-15 min}. Let it rest for {time 5 min} before sliding it out and cutting into wedges.

notes: Leftover wedges keep in the fridge for up to 4 days and are good cold, tucked into a sandwich.
Almost any cooked vegetable works; keep the total to about 3 cups.
